newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end mixed, ACCESS jumps on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end mixed, ACCESS jumps on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Wednesday in a moderate session, then jumped on ACCESS after the AGA report showed an unexpectedly-small weekly gas stock build, industry sources said.

Earlier, November closed 2.7 cents lower at $2.437 per million British thermal units, then jumped to $2.50 on ACCESS shortly after the data. December settled 1.4 cents lower at $2.62. Other deferreds ended narrowly mixed.
"I think it (the AGA build) was the result of the tropical storm, and it's pretty bullish," said one Houston-based trader, noting the number fell well-below expectations.
AGA said U.S. gas inventories rose last week by 38 bcf to 82 percent of capacity, well-below average expectations for a 65-70 bcf weekly stock build, according to an earlier Reuter suvey.
But some objected to the number, noting data for the last two weeks have fallen well outside of expectations.

"You can't print what I think about the number last week or this week. I don't believe them. Where did 60 bcf go? Something should be done to get more credible information," said another Houston-based trader, referring to last week's unexpectedly-high 94 bcf build.
An East Coast trader agreed. "The AGA has lost a lot of credibility after the last two weeks. Both numbers are a joke."

Meanwhile, most discounted Tropical Storm Lili, which at 1400 EDT was stalled 365 miles south-southwest of Havana, Cuba, with winds of about 65 mph. Lili was expected to resume its northward drift and strengthen within the next 24 hours.

And while some still expected storage operators to husband stocks early in the season and prop up the market near-term, others said without colder weather, fading storage demand should put supply and demand out of balance.
Technically, traders still pegged November support in the mid-to-high $2.20s, with resistance seen at today's high of $2.51 and then at the recent high of $2.59.
Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices firmed five to 10 cents Wednesday to the mid-$2.30s or better. Midcon pipes were more than 10 cents higher in the high-$2.20s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip eased 0.3 cent to $2.22. NYMEX said 39,491 Hub contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 34,791.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled two cents higher at $1.075, while deferreds closed up by one-half to 1.5 cents. NYMEX said 23 Alberta contracts traded.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded but November settled two cents higher at $2.14.

On the KCBT, November closed up by 0.9 cent at $2.21, while deferreds ended mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.6 cents to 22.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 501 contracts traded, up from Tuesday's total of 445.
